sentiment.rationale: PepsiCo's Q4 2025 results showed a sequential acceleration in revenue growth and double-digit core EPS growth, but the company's fiscal 2026 guidance was reaffirmed unchanged from the December outlook, not raised. Management expresses confidence in accelerating growth through innovation and affordability investments, but the reaffirmed guidance and cautious language about consumer affordability dynamics prevent a higher score. The score reflects genuine operational momentum (improving North America trends, strong productivity) without a formal guidance raise.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 reported net revenue $29,343 million, up 5.6% year-over-year; full-year 2025 reported net revenue $93,925 million, up 2.3% year-over-year. Organic revenue growth was 2.1% in Q4 and 1.7% for the full year.
summary.eps: Q4 2025 reported GAAP EPS $1.85, up 68% year-over-year; full-year 2025 reported GAAP EPS $6.00, down 14% year-over-year. Q4 2025 core EPS $2.26, up 11% on a constant currency basis; full-year 2025 core EPS $8.14.
summary.guidance: For fiscal 2026, the company expects organic revenue to increase between 2% and 4%, core constant currency EPS to increase between 4% and 6%, a core annual effective tax rate of approximately 22%, capital spending below 5% of net revenue, and a free cash flow conversion ratio of at least 80%. This guidance was affirmed from the December 2025 outlook.
summary.margin: Q4 2025 reported gross margin 53.2%, core gross margin 53.6%; full-year 2025 reported operating margin 12.2%, core operating margin 15.9%. Management noted 'strong operating margin expansion' in Q4.
key_risks: Consumer affordability dynamics, particularly for low- and middle-income consumers in the U.S.
Foreign exchange translation impact (2% on Q4 net revenue, 5% on Q4 EPS).
Higher commodity costs, including tariffs (11-percentage-point impact on PBNA commodity costs in Q4).
Decline in organic volume in PFNA, PBNA, and LatAm Foods.
Impairment charges related to the Rockstar brand ($1.99 billion full-year 2025).
key_opportunities: Accelerating growth through restaging large global brands (Lay's, Gatorade, Quaker).
Product innovation in emerging and functional spaces (fiber, protein, portion control, no artificials).
Sharpening value/affordability initiatives to drive volume and category growth.
Record year of productivity savings to fund investments.
Double-digit shelf space gains for Frito-Lay in retailer resets.
Integration of recent acquisitions (poppi, Siete, Alani Nu) into organic growth.
Improving North America business performance and resilient International business.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Ramon Laguarta stated 'PepsiCo’s fourth quarter results reflected a sequential acceleration... we aim to accelerate growth' and 'we expect North America’s business performance to improve and the International business to remain resilient this year,' conveying confidence in the forward plan.
